newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss unemployment hits post-war high.
newsitem.headline: Swiss unemployment hits post-war high.

text.p: Switzerland reported a record high unemployment rate Thursday in a report highlighting its need for more structural change and a reversal of its protectionist mentality.

Unemployment rose to 5.3 percent in December from 5.1 percent the previous month, the highest monthly rate since World War II, the Swiss Office of Trade, Industry and Labour said. The December rate was marginally higher than expected.
The average jobless rate rose to 4.7 percent for all of 1996 and was likely to rise further in 1997, the office also said.
In addition, the statistics office reported that retail sales in November fell 0.8 percent.
Swiss economic recovery has been hampered for some time by the weak economies of its main trading partners, especially in Europe.

Perhaps just as detrimental, the economists say, are the protectionist attitudes and cartel-like business practices among all but the largest Swiss multi-national corporations -- structural deficiencies that have only now been brought to centre stage by the economy's anaemia.
"The domestic economy has been protected by cartels and has been closed to the rest of Europe," Credit Suisse Research economist Hilda Phan-Huy said.
